name: TeamStarWolf - The Year 2007 in Intrusions
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK Enterprise techniques that the verified 2007 record supports: SecureWorks' Storm Worm analysis (the e-mail dropper, the Overnet-located second stage and the SYN and ICMP floods), Microsoft's MS07-014, MS07-015, MS07-017 and MS07-029 for the Word, Excel, animated cursor and DNS Server RPC flaws exploited at release, US-CERT's alerts on the Solaris telnet worm, the animated cursor, the DNS RPC flaw, malicious PDF files abusing Windows URI handling and the spoofed FTC e-mail, the KEV catalog's CVE-2007 entries, the Justice Department and FBI releases on Soloway and Operations Bot Roast I and II, TJX's filings, the Canadian privacy commissioners' TJX report and the 2008 Gonzalez charges, and the CCDCOE analyses of the Estonia attacks graded Reported. No 2007 source prints an ATT&CK id: every entry is this study's later mapping. The group techniques ATT&CK lists for APT1 are not in this layer. The Stuxnet 0.5 techniques are in the separate ATT&CK for ICS layer navigator/case-studies/chronicle-2007-ics.json. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/CHRONICLE_2007.md. Scores: 70 the source describes the behavior and the study assigns the id, 50 only a Reported source supports the behavior, 40 the mapping is Inferred.

Storm floods on anti-spam sites (12 and 30 Jan); Downey's botnet DDoS (Jun); Goldstein's DDoS on a university (1 Nov, alleged); Estonia (27 Apr to 18 May, Reported) (basis: Described; a later mapping, since no 2007 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [1][47][48][40] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2007.md.

Storm ICMP floods (Jan); Estonia ping floods, including Galushkevich's admitted attacks (Reported) (basis: Described; a later mapping, since no 2007 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [1][40][41] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2007.md.

Storm TCP SYN floods on port 80 (Jan); ATT&CK places SYN floods under this sub-technique, and assigning it here is this study's reading (basis: Described; a later mapping, since no 2007 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [1] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2007.md.

Estonia: floods against government, e-banking and news web services; the sources do not describe the flood type at the service layer (basis: Inferred; a later mapping, since no 2007 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [40][41] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2007.md.

Storm's dropper, an e-mail virus (Jan, mass mailing rather than targeted; the attachment form is not in the analysis as verified, so this part is Inferred); spoofed FTC e-mail with malicious attachments (30 Oct) (basis: Described; a later mapping, since no 2007 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [1][32] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2007.md.

Storm's botnets (Jan to Feb); Soloway's spam relayed through botnets (alleged, to May); the Bot Roast cases (Jun, Nov); Estonia (Reported; whether the bots were compromised or rented is not established) (basis: Described; a later mapping, since no 2007 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [1][46][47][48][40][41] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2007.md.

TJX: intruder may have entered through store wireless networks (Canadian commissioners, 25 Sep); wardriving into retailers' wireless networks (DOJ, 2008, alleged); FTC alleges wireless access was not limited (basis: Described; a later mapping, since no 2007 source prints an ATT&CK id). Sources [5][10][8] refer to the Sources table of case-studies/CHRONICLE_2007.md.
